<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by making the live comparison easier to decide: who may keep irrigating, and whether those gallons are recovered this month. After A admitted prices need not stop paying irrigators and allowances should not be set to close the shortage, B turned that into a coherent “rationing by wallet / waste for sale” weighing that A never fully neutralized. A’s best hit—that B would still ban even if aggregate savings were met—was real, but B’s distribution, timing, and main-instrument replies did more damage across the later rounds.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2 after the pressure questions: using A’s A1/A2 concessions (do not recover the wealthy household’s gallons; do not set the allowance tight enough to close the shortage) to argue that the “backstop” ban is the instrument that actually delivers the water.</best_rebuttal>
